Source.aws_documentation_revision: AWS live documentation; immutable revision not exposed

captures.raw_xml: Every native response has raw_xml_path. CLI-side validation failures have no HTTP response/XML. Debug authentication logs were discarded, never persisted.

vpc: CreateVpc canonicalized 10.237.19.7/20 to 10.237.16.0/20; create returned pending, next describe available. CIDR association already associated.
Separate owned VPCs with identical CIDRs succeeded. Overlap is not an account-wide VPC uniqueness constraint.
DNS support true, DNS hostnames false initially; enable hostnames mutation described true.
CreateTags merges and replaces values; DeleteTags with a nonmatching value leaves the tag; deleting key without value removes it.

Deleting a VPC with owned subnets returned DependencyViolation. Deleting the emptied VPC removed its provider-created default SG, main route table and default ACL; explicit subsequent IDs returned NotFound.
subnet: CreateSubnet canonicalized 10.237.16.7/28 to 10.237.16.0/28 with 11 available IPv4 addresses; /24 returned 251. Both created subnets were available immediately.
Explicit us-east-1a mapped to use1-az6 in this account. Omitted zone selected the same zone, not round-robin. Do not universalize account-specific AZ name mappings.
Overlapping subnet -> InvalidSubnet.Conflict; outside VPC and /29 -> InvalidSubnet.Range.
MapPublicIpOnLaunch initially false; modification true was observable via DescribeSubnets and restored false. No public address was allocated. EnableDns64 false mutation succeeded.
Mixed existing/missing explicit IDs failed the whole DescribeSubnets request, rather than returning a partial list.
security_groups: Default VPC-created SG has self-referencing all-protocol ingress and all-IPv4 egress. A custom SG begins with empty ingress and all-IPv4 egress. SG rules have independent native IDs/ARNs.
Custom group name is unique within VPC, not account: duplicate same-VPC name -> InvalidGroup.Duplicate; same name in another owned VPC succeeded.
Ingress/egress CIDRs canonicalize before duplicate detection; duplicate -> InvalidPermission.Duplicate. Rule-description updates by rule ID are visible in DescribeSecurityGroupRules.

Revoke by canonical CIDR without description succeeds despite a stored description. Repeating revoke in this nondefault VPC -> InvalidPermission.NotFound. Missing rule ID -> InvalidSecurityGroupRuleId.NotFound.

Same-VPC group reference resolves owner metadata and blocks deleting the referenced SG (DependencyViolation). Cross-VPC unpeered reference -> InvalidGroup.NotFound with message that resources belong to different networks.
DescribeSecurityGroups synthetic sg-00000000000000000 -> InvalidGroupId.Malformed, but real deleted IDs -> InvalidGroup.NotFound. Preserve operation/input-specific error distinctions.
routing_acl: Main route table exposes a Main=true association with no SubnetId; implicit subnet routing does not add explicit table associations. Default ACL does gain explicit subnet associations.

Both main and custom route tables start with active local VPC CIDR route, Origin=CreateRouteTable. No internet route or gateway exists in these probes; local reachability must not imply internet egress.
Custom route-table association exposes Main=false and concrete SubnetId; deleting while associated -> DependencyViolation; disassociate then delete succeeds.
Default ACL has all-IPv4 allow rule 100 and deny rule 32767 in each direction. Custom ACL initially has only deny 32767 in each direction.

Custom ACL protocol 6 TCP entry canonicalizes CIDR. Repeating identical CreateNetworkAclEntry succeeded (not duplicate error). Replace changed allow to deny; repeat delete -> InvalidNetworkAclEntry.NotFound.
CreateNetworkAcl projected empty IcmpTypeCode and PortRange structures for default deny rules; DescribeNetworkAcls omitted them. Preserve response-specific absence.
pagination: MaxResults minimum 5: CLI rejects 1 before HTTP, while direct signed request returns HTTP400 InvalidParameterValue.
MaxResults combined with explicit SG or subnet IDs -> InvalidParameterCombination.

Seven SGs returned page sizes 5 then 2, but second SG page STILL included a nonempty NextToken. Follow tokens, not page length. Reusing first token returned the same resource page but a different continuation token.
Six subnets returned 5 then 1; second subnet page omitted NextToken and replay was byte-equivalent at decoded-output level.

Changing filters with an SG token -> InvalidParameterValue; changing filters with a subnet token succeeded with empty Subnets and a NextToken. Do not impose a uniform cross-operation token/filter rule.
Continuation captures explicitly marked post-cleanup must not be confused with the original live-resource pages.
query_wire: EC2 success root is operation-specific in namespace http://ec2.amazonaws.com/doc/2016-11-15/ with requestId. Error root is unnamespaced Response/Errors/Error/{Code,Message} and RequestID (capital ID). No IAM-style Type element was present.
DescribeVpcs/Subnets accept GET and POST, unindexed list values, zero/non-1/gapped indexes, and leading-zero indexes. Filter indexes and filter value indexes may also start at 0 or 2.
Wrong member casing -> UnknownParameter. Negative index -> InvalidParameterValue for illegal XML character. Nonnumeric list index bound an empty ID and produced NotFound.

Repeated scalar Filter.1.Name: POST uses LAST value; GET uses FIRST value. Calls 55-56,59-64 isolate valid versus invalid filter in both orders. wire_parameters records actual transmission order; early GET signing probes sorted query pairs before transmitting.

Authorized DryRun create/delete returns HTTP412 DryRunOperation. Describe after dry-run delete confirmed resource still existed. No scoped denial policy was introduced, so these captures do not prove IAM denial precedence.

cleanup.resource_absence: Each tracked VPC/subnet/SG/route table/ACL, including provider-created defaults, returned its service-specific NotFound after deletion. Final tag-filter describes across all five resource types returned empty collections.
cleanup.metadata_not_resources: Native IDs/ARNs/CIDR associations/rule IDs remain in immutable JSON/XML evidence only. The shared DhcpOptionsId observed in VPC output was preexisting account metadata, not an owned resource; it was neither modified nor deleted.
cleanup.cost_scope: No instances, ENIs, public IP allocations, NAT gateways, endpoints, load balancers, or paid compute were created. Only VPC/subnet/SG/custom route-table/custom ACL controls were mutated.
cleanup.capture_retry: First attempt stopped at local CLI MaxResults validation, cleaned its VPC, then resumed with validation failures retained. The historical probe_exception refers only to that cleaned first attempt; later full runs and cleanup succeeded.

ecs_selection_implications: Resolve subnet and SG IDs in account/region scope and require compatible VPC ownership; names and CIDRs are not globally unique keys.
Account-specific AZ identity and available IPv4 capacity belong to subnet metadata; five IPv4 addresses are reserved before workload allocation.
Subnet route-table selection needs explicit association or fallback to the VPC main table; ACL association and direction rules are separate from stateful SG permissions.
The probes exercised network control semantics only, not ECS task execution or real packet delivery. No claim of ECS runtime connectivity is made.
